title: OpenStax says Piaget called 2- and 3-year-olds unaware of other viewpoints
summary: OpenStax says Piaget described 2- to 3-year-olds as egocentric, meaning not yet aware of other people's points of view.
body: The lifespan chapter recalls Piaget's description of 2- to 3-year-olds as egocentric: they do not have an awareness of others' points of view. The sentence is the textbook's report of Piaget, not a new experiment and not a claim that a toddler is selfish. The next change, understanding that other people have different thoughts, is a separate statement about ages 3 to 5. A label from one theorist is not a diagnosis.

sources.note: Paraphrase only, no quotation. OpenStax Psychology web chapter at /books/psychology/, credited as the first-edition path (CC BY 4.0). Supports the report that Piaget described 2- to 3-year-olds as egocentric, without awareness of others' points of view.
